subject: Mediation analysis of a panel data - using Lavaan - Help needed

messages.author: 9d9c5320ccdc0622
messages.subject: Mediation analysis of a panel data - using Lavaan - Help needed
parts:
Dear Sir

I want to conduct a mediation analysis for panel data set. The variables have been made using secondary data.

Panel size: T = 10 and number of firms = 355.

My suspected mediating variable is a psychological variable.

I am using "Lavaan" package with following R code:
##PVCX100 is a mediator; REO is DV; logPDD_HA and HPD_A are explanatory variables

Model1 <- 'PVCX100 ~ logPDD_HA + HPD_A
            REO ~ PVCX100 + logPDD_HA + HPD_A'

fit1=sem(Model1,data = D1,na.rm=TRUE)

summary(fit1)

I got following result:

summary(fit1)

  Number of observations                          1723        3545

  REO ~

    logPDD_HA        -0.009    0.004   -2.027    0.043
    HPD_A            -0.001    0.001   -1.772    0.076

Variances:

   .PVCX100           0.421    0.014   29.351    0.000
   .REO               0.014    0.000   29.351    0.000

I have following questions:
1. Can you use above code to find mediation in panel data? If yes, what happens to unobserved individual heterogeneity.

2. Do I need to include the control variables in the regression model?

2. If above method is correct, what should we conclude from the output?

In case of HPD_A, there is no mediation. But in case of logPDD_HA, can we conclude a partial mediation?

I thank you in advance.

Best regards

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Mediation analysis of a panel data - using Lavaan - Help needed
parts: Panel size: T = 10 and number of firms = 355.
Does that mean 10 time points?  You only model a single instance of each variable below, so is this only using 1 timepoint?
1. Can you use above code to find mediation in panel data?

You can, if you label the parameters and define the indirect effect(s) you want to use to test mediation.

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/mediation.html
If yes, what happens to unobserved individual heterogeneity.

What do you mean?   Have you stacked all timepoints on top of each other in "long" format, so that each person has T = 10 rows of data?  If so, then this analysis is invalid because you are not accounting for observations being nested within individuals.  You could fit a multilevel SEM, which is very experimental at this point, or you could put the data in wide format (355 independent rows, so no issue with latent heterogeneity) and run a cross-lagged panel model.
2. Do I need to include the control variables in the regression model?
Depends on your theory and the background literature.  This isn't a software question.
2. If above method is correct, what should we conclude from the output? In case of HPD_A, there is no mediation. But in case of logPDD_HA, can we conclude a partial mediation?

Again, read the tutorial I linked to, showing you how to calculate indirect effects that you want to test.  Other than that, your other questions lead me to believe you should read a lot more about mediation models to inform how you specify them and draw inferences from them.  Other than textbooks and articles, SEMNET is a good resource for general SEM questions like that:

www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
